independent_reviewer_counterclaim: THE STRONGEST CASE AGAINST THIS BATCH IS THAT ITS HEADLINE IS A CLAIM ABOUT A STANDARD-SETTING PROCESS THAT IT DID NOT OBSERVE. I establish that REF-01005 measured 1:12 as unnegotiable by close to half its wheelchair-user sample, and that the report series was commissioned to improve ANSI A117.1. I DO NOT ESTABLISH THAT A117.1 SET 1:12 IN SPITE OF THIS FINDING, because I have not read A117.1's deliberations, its dates, or what value it carried before 1979. The adjacency is suggestive and it is not a causal record, and a reader who takes 'the code ignored its own evidence' from this batch has taken more than the bytes support. SECOND, THE 1:20 FIGURE RESTS ON THREE PEOPLE. The escalation design sent only failures upward, so 'every wheelchair user completed 40 feet at 1:20' has a denominator of three, and the sentence reads universal while the number does not. I have written that into the extraction note rather than the headline, but the headline is what gets quoted. THIRD, THE CONVERGENCE I CALL STRUCTURAL IS ONE DOCUMENT. Walter 1971 and Steinfeld 1979 agreeing at 1:16 is Steinfeld's report of Walter; until Walter is retrieved, counting it as two independent findings is lens L3, and the temptation to do so will grow as the finding is repeated. FOURTH, AND MOST LIKELY TO BITE: I extended db.py three times in a research batch. Each was justified by a live refusal and an owner rule, none was speculative, and all three went through the sanctioned path -- but a batch that repairs its own tooling is a batch whose scope grew while nobody was gating it, and the honest reading is that the research half of this batch is one admission.

bias_direction: TOWARD THE DRAMATIC READING OF A GOOD FIND. The retrieval succeeded after two batches of nulls, and the finding -- that the measurement behind an accessibility standard did not support the standard -- is the most quotable thing this project has produced. That is precisely the condition under which a batch overstates. The specific pressures: (1) to narrate 'the code ignored its own evidence' when what I hold is adjacency, not a deliberative record; (2) to treat the Walter/Steinfeld agreement as two independent findings when it is one document reporting another; (3) to let '1:20 worked for everyone' travel without its denominator of three; (4) to read the study's high-control design as earning T1, because a T1 admission would have unblocked the determination this project has been stuck on -- which the owner ruling refused, and which I record as having been MY inclination before the ruling arrived rather than a temptation I resisted unaided. The counter-pressure applied is that each of these is written into the row notes at the point the claim is made, not quarantined in a caveats section.
